title: Naruto
description: Japanese manga series by Masashi Kishimoto
wiki_lead:
Naruto is a Japanese manga series written and illustrated by Masashi Kishimoto. It tells the story of Naruto Uzumaki, a young, socially isolated ninja who seeks recognition from his peers and dreams of becoming the Hokage, the leader of his village. The story is told in two parts: the first is set in Naruto's pre-teen years (volumes 1–27), and the second in his teens (volumes 28–72). The series is based on two one-shot manga by Kishimoto: Karakuri (1995), which earned Kishimoto an honorable mention in Shueisha's monthly Hop Step Award the following year, and Naruto (1997).
Naruto was serialized in Shueisha's shōnen manga magazine Weekly Shōnen Jump from September 1999 to November 2014, with its 700 chapters collected in 72 tankōbon volumes. Viz Media licensed the manga for North American production and serialized Naruto in their digital Weekly Shonen Jump magazine. The manga was adapted into two anime television series by Pierrot and Aniplex, which ran from October 2002 to March 2017 on TV Tokyo. Pierrot also produced 11 animated films and 12 original video animations (OVAs). The franchise additionally includes light novels, video games, and trading cards. The story continues in Boruto, where Naruto's son Boruto Uzumaki creates his own ninja path as opposed to following his father's.
Naruto is one of the best-selling manga series of all time, having sold over 250 million copies in 46 countries. It has become one of Viz Media's best-selling manga series; their English translations of the volumes have appeared on USA Today and The New York Times's bestseller list several times, and the seventh volume won a Quill Award in 2006. Naruto has been praised for its character development, storylines, and action sequences, though some felt the latter slowed the story down. Critics noted that the manga, which contains coming-of-age themes, often incorporates cultural references to Japanese mythology and Confucianism.

Plot


Part I

A demonic nine-tailed fox called Kurama attacks Konoha, the Village Hidden in the Leaves in the Land of Fire, one of the Five Great Shinobi Countries in the Ninja World. In response, the leader of the Leaf, Fourth Hokage Minato Namikaze, sacrifices his life by splitting the fox in half and sealing the fox inside himself and in the body of his newborn son, Naruto Uzumaki, respectively, making him a host of the beast. The Third Hokage, Hiruzen Sarutobi, returns from retirement to become the leader of the Leaf again. Naruto is often scorned by Konoha's villagers for being the host of the Nine-Tails. Due to a decree by the Third Hokage forbidding any mention of these events, Naruto learns nothing about the Nine-Tails until 12 years later, when Mizuki, a renegade ninja, reveals the truth to him. Naruto defeats Mizuki in combat, earning the respect of his teacher, Iruka Umino.

grok_lead: Naruto is a Japanese manga series written and illustrated by Masashi Kishimoto, chronicling the coming-of-age story of its titular protagonist, Naruto Uzumaki, a young orphan and aspiring ninja in the fictional Hidden Leaf Village who seeks to earn the respect of his peers and become Hokageâthe village's leaderâdespite being shunned for harboring the Nine-Tailed Fox, a powerful demon sealed within him since birth. The narrative explores themes of perseverance, friendship, and redemption as Naruto forms bonds with teammates Sasuke Uchiha and Sakura Haruno under the guidance of their sensei, Kakashi Hatake, while confronting escalating threats from rival villages, rogue ninjas, and internal conflicts that test the ninja world's fragile peace. The anime adaptation, produced by Studio Pierrot and Aniplex, faithfully expanded the manga 's world across two main series: the original Naruto, which aired 220 episodes on TV Tokyo from October 2002 to February 2007, covering Naruto's early years as a genin ninja, and its sequel Naruto: ShippÅ«den, which ran for 500 episodes from February 2007 to March 2017, depicting his growth into a more powerful jÅnin amid a looming global war. Both anime series, directed by Hayato Date, incorporated filler arcs to extend the storyline beyond the manga while maintaining its core focus on intense battles, character development, and the philosophy of the "Will of Fire" that unites the Hidden Leaf Village. Naruto 's enduring legacy extends beyond print and animation to include eleven theatrical films, numerous video games, novels, and merchandise, with its influence evident in the 2016 sequel manga Boruto: Naruto Next Generations, supervised by Kishimoto, which shifts the spotlight to Naruto's son and a new generation of ninjas navigating a modernized ninja world.
